verdictExplanation: The system rejects applicants on its own and scores employee sentiment from workplace messages, which puts it at indicative tier IV. OIPC BC regards continuous, routine employee monitoring as seldom authorized, so the sentiment scoring is a blocker as designed. The redesign path is to drop the continuous sentiment scoring, limit any measurement to a narrow and overt purpose, and keep a person in each hiring decision.

intake.title: Applicant screening and team sentiment scoring
intake.processDescription: Recruiters at a regional logistics company read several hundred applications for each warehouse and driver posting and shortlist candidates by hand. Separately, team leads try to spot disengagement through one-to-ones. We want a vendor's machine-learning tool to rank applicants and automatically reject those below a cut-off, and to score employee sentiment continuously from workplace chat messages so HR can flag low performers and disengaged staff for follow-up.

subtasks.name: Parse applications
subtasks.description: Extract work history, licences and availability from each application.
subtasks.rationale: Field extraction; errors can unfairly drop an applicant if not checked.

subtasks.name: Score and rank applicants
subtasks.description: Score each applicant against the role profile and rank the pool.
subtasks.rationale: The ranking decides who is considered for the job.

subtasks.name: Auto-reject below cut-off
subtasks.description: Send a rejection to applicants whose score falls below the cut-off.
subtasks.rationale: A rejection is a decision about a person with no human in the loop.

subtasks.name: Score employee sentiment
subtasks.description: Score sentiment continuously from workplace chat messages for each employee.
subtasks.rationale: Continuous monitoring of individual employees that feeds HR follow-up.

subtasks.name: Flag low performers
subtasks.description: Combine sentiment and productivity signals to flag employees for HR follow-up.
subtasks.rationale: A flag can lead to performance action against an employee.

assumptions: The vendor hosts the tool in Canada.
clarifyingQuestions: Are employees told that their messages are scored?
